image_description: A large, mature common iguana (Iguana iguana) resting on the ground amidst leaf litter and low-lying vegetation. The iguana has a robust body with greyish-green coloration and distinct orange/reddish hues on its lower jaw and limbs. It features a prominent dorsal crest of spine-like scales running from the neck down the back. The head is large and triangular with visible granular scales and a subtympanic shield. The tail is long and thick, extending towards the right side of the frame, partially obscured by foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, exhibiting the characteristic triangular shape and large size relative to the body. A dewlap structure is visible under the chin/jaw area, consistent with an adult male iguana.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, circular scale characteristic of the subtympanic shield is clearly visible on the side of the head, below the ear region.
The torso of the iguana is thick and muscular, fitting the description of a robust body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana displays adult coloration: primarily greyish-green with some darker banding and significant orange/red pigmentation on the lower parts, which is common in mature males.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A very prominent, continuous row of spike-like scales runs along the spine from the neck down the back. This is a defining feature and is clearly present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture of the skin shows fine granularity on the body and larger, smoother plates on the head, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the forelimb is visible and appears muscular, the feet/digits are largely obscured by leaves and shadow. It is impossible to definitively count five clawed digits or verify their structure without speculation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending behind the body. It appears thick at the base and tapers. While the full length isn't visible to compare exactly to the body, the visible portion shows the correct lateral compression and scaling pattern.
